verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's core design lets developers call any provider through one interface and issue virtual keys that map to underlying provider credentials, with per-key spend/model access control ('Put your full AI stack behind one key', virtual key docs) — implying BYOK usage. However, the evidence pack lacks an explicit walkthrough of adding a personal provider API key to the proxy config and having it used for a developer's own traffic, and there is no independent confirmation of this specific flow. Missing for 10: explicit BYOK config example, independent/hands-on confirmation of per-developer key routing.
